doses.title: Feel it, don't become it
doses.reflection: An emotion can be important without being the full truth about you or the world. Give it attention, not the microphone all day.
doses.question: What feeling needs care rather than a verdict?

doses.title: The story and the sensation
doses.reflection: A tight chest is a sensation; the story about what it means is another layer. Notice both separately.
doses.question: What is happening in your body, and what are you telling yourself?

doses.title: Welcome the resistance
doses.reflection: If you cannot welcome a feeling, begin with the part of you that doesn't want it. There's room for that too.
doses.question: What would it feel like to welcome your resistance?

doses.title: Wonder over judgment
doses.reflection: Curiosity can turn an inner critic into a question. Ask what is happening before deciding it is wrong.
doses.question: What would you ask if you were genuinely curious?

doses.title: The young feeling
doses.reflection: A strong reaction can make you feel very young. Meet it with patience instead of embarrassment.
doses.question: What reassurance might this part of you need?

doses.title: Listening to anger
doses.reflection: Anger may point toward an unmet need or a crossed boundary. Hear its message before choosing what to do.
doses.question: What is this anger trying to protect?

doses.title: A safer conversation
doses.reflection: You can describe your experience without declaring the other person's intentions. Honest language leaves room for repair.
doses.question: Can you start a sentence with 'I noticed'?

doses.title: No need to argue with sadness
doses.reflection: When sadness arrives, it may need companionship more than a strategy. Be with it for a moment.
doses.question: What would it mean to sit beside this sadness?

doses.title: Feelings aren't instructions
doses.reflection: Fear can be real and worthy of care without requiring every action it suggests. Slow down before deciding.
doses.question: What action serves your values rather than your fear?

doses.title: The art of repair
doses.reflection: Being close to people means sometimes getting it wrong. A sincere repair matters more than a polished defense.
doses.question: What would a simple repair sound like?

doses.title: Meet the protector
doses.reflection: Defensiveness often tries to keep something tender safe. Thank that impulse, then ask whether it still helps.
doses.question: What is your defensiveness protecting?

doses.title: Be curious in conflict
doses.reflection: Two people can be uncomfortable without either being the villain. Curiosity can create the first bit of space.
doses.question: What experience might the other person be having?

doses.title: Name it softly
doses.reflection: Saying 'I'm disappointed' can be more connecting than hiding that feeling behind criticism.
doses.question: What feeling could you name without blame?

doses.title: An honest request
doses.reflection: People cannot reliably meet needs they don't know about. A direct, kind request gives connection a chance.
doses.question: What could you ask for clearly?

doses.title: Make space for joy
doses.reflection: You may be practiced at examining pain and forget to fully feel happiness. Let a good moment land.
doses.question: What joy is asking for your attention?

doses.title: The fear beneath control
doses.reflection: When you want to manage every detail, notice what feels unsafe about not knowing.
doses.question: What fear might be underneath the urge to control?

doses.title: Allow a messy answer
doses.reflection: When someone asks how you are, your truthful answer can be more complex than 'fine.' You get to choose whom to trust with it.
doses.question: Who feels safe enough for an honest answer?

doses.title: The compassion experiment
doses.reflection: Try treating your difficult emotion as you would a frightened friend. Notice whether your inner tone changes.
doses.question: How would you speak to a friend feeling this?

doses.title: Let the body speak
doses.reflection: Before explaining why you're upset, notice where the feeling lives physically. Sensation may slow the story down.
doses.question: Where does this feeling have a shape?

doses.title: Curiosity for yourself
doses.reflection: You are allowed to wonder about your behavior without turning every insight into a criticism.
doses.question: What are you learning about your reactions?

doses.title: A request, not a test
doses.reflection: Instead of secretly testing whether someone will read your mind, consider asking openly for what matters.
doses.question: What need could become a kind request?

doses.title: Beyond blame
doses.reflection: Blame may offer a quick story, but understanding gives you more choices. Try asking what led to this moment.
doses.question: What might be more useful than finding fault?

doses.title: The uncomfortable pause
doses.reflection: Silence during a hard conversation can feel risky. It can also give both people room to think.
doses.question: What would happen if you paused before replying?

doses.title: A softer inner dialogue
doses.reflection: When your inner voice gets harsh, notice its fear underneath the criticism. You can respond with steadiness.
doses.question: What concern is hiding beneath the harsh words?

doses.title: Thank the feeling
doses.reflection: An emotion might be trying to help, even if its strategy isn't useful. Acknowledge the signal without obeying every suggestion.
doses.question: What is this feeling attempting to do for you?

doses.title: Choose connection
doses.reflection: Winning an argument may leave you lonely. Notice when understanding matters more than scoring a point.
doses.question: What would help both people feel heard?

doses.title: Stay with the tenderness
doses.reflection: A vulnerable truth may be hiding beneath sarcasm or irritation. Find a safe way to say it directly.
doses.question: What honest feeling is hard to share?

doses.title: Notice the shutdown
doses.reflection: Wanting to withdraw can be a signal that you need safety or rest. Give yourself space and communicate it kindly.
doses.question: What kind of pause would help you return?

doses.title: The simple apology
doses.reflection: A clear apology doesn't need five excuses attached. Own your part and listen to its impact.
doses.question: What could you take responsibility for?

doses.title: A boundary without a story
doses.reflection: You don't have to build a case that someone is bad to know something doesn't work for you.
doses.question: What boundary is true without an accusation?

doses.title: Room for two truths
doses.reflection: You can be hurt by someone and still care about them. Complexity doesn't mean your boundaries must disappear.
doses.question: Which two feelings can you hold together?

doses.title: Let yourself be supported
doses.reflection: Independence is valuable, but receiving care is not a failure. Give someone a chance to show up.
doses.question: What support could you receive today?

doses.title: Unlearn the performance
doses.reflection: You don't need to seem unbothered to deserve respect. Authentic calm leaves room for the truth.
doses.question: Where are you pretending not to feel?

doses.title: The mindful disagreement
doses.reflection: Differences need not destroy connection. Ask a sincere question before defending your view.
doses.question: What would help you understand their perspective?

doses.title: Feel first, decide later
doses.reflection: Big feelings can make decisions seem urgent. When safe, give yourself time to settle before making a choice.
doses.question: What decision could benefit from a pause?

doses.title: A new response to shame
doses.reflection: Shame often asks you to hide. Consider offering yourself the same dignity you'd offer another person.
doses.question: What truth can you meet without humiliation?

doses.title: Start with wonder
doses.reflection: If you're stuck in self-criticism, try replacing 'What's wrong with me?' with 'What's happening for me?'
doses.question: What becomes possible with that question?
